title: A Gantt you can drag, and tickets that run themselves

items.words: Gantt charts are plain Markdown you drag: move, resize and link tasks, and old Mermaid gantts convert in a tap.
Cycles with a burndown, estimates and velocity, epics and milestones, and priority chips with stale marks.
My tickets across every notebook, a Triage list worked by keys, and bulk edits with one Undo.
Coloured labels and components on tickets, filterable and groupable everywhere.
Rules like "When status becomes Done, post to Slack", GitHub PRs on tickets, and Start/Stop timers.
Watch tickets to hear of changes, see each ticket's history, and get a morning digest of what's due.
Possible duplicates are shown, and Merge into… moves comments and links with one Undo.

title: Twelve new things for your notes

items.words: Notes show "Linked from" at their foot, and ![[Note#Heading]] shows a section as a live card.
Headings fold from the gutter, and <details> blocks are toggles you can add from the +.
Queries can be a calendar, a timeline or a chart, with rollups across linked notes.
Folders and notebooks can have a template, and buttons in a note run an action.
Tickets get sub-tickets with a progress bar, and blocked tickets ask before they're done.
Type @ to mention a teammate or a day, and verify a page as the team's current truth.
Share a form anyone can fill in: answers arrive sealed and land as tickets.
Under Claude's reply, a card lists every note it made or changed, New or Changed; tap one to open it.
Copy link on each of those notes puts its share link on the clipboard.
Meetings Ghost's bot is in (Google Meet and Zoom) show their transcript live, named and timed, while the call runs.
Meetings recorded on your phone show live words under the cassette and in Transcript while the screen is on.
Settings › Recording › Live transcript during meetings: on the phone it runs while charging unless you choose otherwise.
A meeting's note is there from its first words, so you can write in it during the call.

title: What's new, and comments in the margin

items.words: What's new in Ghost.md shows after every update, with a full changelog in Settings › About.
Hover a line to comment on it: a comment glyph appears in the margin beside it.
Lines with comments show their count in the margin, and a click opens the thread.
Downloads in the activity ring show just their arrow, without a second progress circle inside the ring.
Meeting transcripts are split into turns, each one starting with who spoke and when.
A meeting's note has Note and Transcript buttons, so the transcript stays out of the way while you write.
In Transcript, the turn being heard is lit, and tapping a turn plays the recording from there.
Rebuild, on a meeting's tape, writes the transcript's turns again from what was recorded.
Finding words that are in the transcript opens Transcript right at that turn.
The header's ••• menu shows each row's coloured icon in the default layout too.
App updates now live in the activity tray, with a green badge on the ring when one is waiting.
Work a plugin is doing wears that plugin's own logo in the tray and its chips.
Settings › About keeps your version, and Check for updates opens the tray to show what it found.
When nothing is running, the activity ring holds a grey check: all done and in sync.
The activity ring is always in the header, grey when nothing is happening.
All notes by folder and New note are now the first two rows of the header's ••• menu.
The sync's bar fills as your notes sync instead of spinning.
The sync's bar no longer sits full while there's still more to sync.
Grouped command is now the header's default layout.
The home page always has a way to search, whichever header you use.
Result chips never cover a page's own buttons, like Hide or Stop.
An activity ring in the header shows what Ghost.md is working on, in colour, with a tray of the details.
The tray lists running, waiting and failed work, and what was done today and over the past week.
Finished work leaves a small result chip with a way to open it.
Notes waiting to sync wear a small arrow by their title, and uploads show a thin bar as they go.
A meeting's summary streams into its note as it is written, and header images shimmer where they'll land.
Progress shows outside the app too: Android notifications, the Mac's Dock and menu bar, and iPhone Live Activities.
Big jobs ask before they start, with their cost, and Calm draws all of it in ink.
A meeting is one note on every device: the summary at the top, the transcript below and the recording with it.
A meeting's summary no longer goes missing when the transcript arrives from another device.
Opening your own meeting's share link opens the meeting itself, not a "(shared)" copy.
A summary that still hasn't arrived ten minutes later is written again.
Long meetings sync faster and use far less memory on your phone.
A note dragged out of an organization stays safe, even if another of your devices runs an older version.
For two weeks after a move, your up-to-date devices put the note back if an older one removes it.
Words you wrote in the note meanwhile are kept, not an older copy.
Dragging a note or a folder into or out of an organization now asks to confirm instead of refusing.
The question says who will be able to read and edit it before anything moves.
It works from folder tiles, the folder strip, the workspace pills and the sidebar alike.
Links in a notebook open with a tap, in its own words and in its pages.
Shared notes on the web open in a clean Read view, with a Markdown toggle for the source.
In the web's Read view, to-dos line up with the bullets around them.
Tapping or clicking a link in a note opens it, instead of putting the cursor in it.
Links inside a table's cells open with a tap too.
To edit a link, tap just after it, use the arrow keys, or press and hold.
On a Mac, Cmd-click opens a link even while you're editing it.
Plugins wear their companies' real logos, like Notion, GitHub, Todoist and Discord.
Zoom's plugin shows a video camera, drawn in your chosen icon pack.
Google Meet's logo is shown in white on its own colour, and the Meetings page has a plain meetings icon.
A shared meeting can carry its recording, so anyone with the link can listen along.
The shared page plays the cassette and lights each part of the transcript as it's heard.
Switch a shared meeting between Summary and Transcript, with who spoke and when on every turn.
Meeting recordings sync, so any of your devices can share one.
The command search finds every setting and every plugin, not just your notes.
Choosing a setting from the search opens Settings right at it, lit up so you can spot it.
Searching Settings stays quick as you type each letter.
The Aster plugin brings Aster's models to Ghost.md with your own Aster key.
Type the name of any model Aster offers, even one that isn't in its list yet.
The spending meter counts Aster's work at Aster's own prices.
Every plugin you set up now has a short spoken setup that walks you through it.
Notion, Google Calendar and GitHub sign in and check the connection right inside their setup.
Keyboard modes needs nothing set up: pick Vim or Emacs on its page.
OpenAI, Gemini and any OpenAI-compatible model can now be added as plugins beside Claude.
Settings › AI › Assistant chooses which model answers your chats and which writes up your meetings.
The Keyboard modes plugin brings Vim or Emacs keys to your notes on a hardware keyboard.
Signing in to Notion works again.
A folder button by Home opens all your notes by folder, in the icon view.
On a desktop, the dock rests at its small size.
The Filters panel no longer clips the row you've chosen.
